items.titleZh: 美国大奖赛后维斯塔潘与哈贾尔对红牛表达不满
items.summaryZh: 美国大奖赛后，维斯塔潘和哈贾尔因起步不佳、无线电通讯问题以及两停策略选择对红牛表达强烈不满，维斯塔潘认为两停策略让一停的安东内利拿下胜利。
items.originalTitle: Why US GP has left Verstappen and Hadjar furious at Red Bull
items.summaryEn: After the United States Grand Prix, Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar voiced strong frustration with Red Bull over poor starts, radio communication problems and the two-stop strategy call, with Verstappen believing it opened the door for one-stopping Kimi Antonelli to win.
detailZh: 美国大奖赛后，马克斯·维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔因一系列本可避免的问题对红牛表达强烈不满，这些问题让他们无法充分发挥赛车的潜力。
起步阶段就出了问题，维斯塔潘和哈贾尔分别从第二位和第三位发车，但起步表现不佳。
随后两人在整场比赛中都受到无线电问题的困扰，与维修区墙的沟通变得困难；同时维斯塔潘对两停策略的选择感到恼火，这一选择让一停的基米·安东内利得以拿下统治性胜利。
尽管车队领队洛朗·梅基斯在冲线后立即通过无线电承认车队有"几件事需要整理"，但驾驶舱内的沮丧情绪显然十分强烈。
在拿下第三名冲过终点线后，维斯塔潘在赛后一段语气低沉的无线电信息中说：“太糟糕了：速度、错误的轮胎、糟糕的进站、糟糕的发动机制动。什么都不管用。”
赛后接受Viaplay采访时，被问及是否同意在第二段 stint 中改用软胎、而当时看起来更应该使用更硬配方轮胎的策略决定，维斯塔潘说：“不，并没有达成一致。这就是我不理解的原因。那样的话，所有人都会知道我们要执行两停。”
随后，在提到平衡和发动机制动方面的挣扎——而持续的无线电问题让情况雪上加霜——维斯塔潘讽刺地对媒体说：“也许我们干脆开始用手语交流算了。那样可能还更便宜。”
“这是一场灾难。说实话，真的非常令人沮丧。”
哈贾尔更加愤怒，他暗示红牛需要重新设计离合器，因为起步多次乏力。
“需要重新设计，因为目前它太脆弱了，”最终以第六名完赛的哈贾尔说道。“它无法很好地应对温度。这真的很艰难。”
随后，他对车队无线电这样相对简单的事情为何会成为如此令人沮丧的问题表示困惑。
“目前我们连小事都做不好，”他说。“我的无线电很差，我甚至不知道发生了什么。我松开离合器，结果就变成了一场噩梦。
“我们把这两个问题解决掉，可能就能登上领奖台了。看起来最难的事情我们能做到，而那些愚蠢的小事却做不到。”
梅基斯很清楚这些问题，它们让原本可能的胜利挑战变成了车手们一个令人沮丧的下午。
关于维斯塔潘的策略决定，红牛表示需要分析为什么第二段 stint（ stint）的轮胎退化如此严重，考虑到比赛开局阶段与安东内利的对抗看起来相当势均力敌。
被问及维斯塔潘的抱怨时，梅基斯说：“我不确定他指的是什么，因为我没有听到他说的话，但我觉得可能让他感到意外的一件事是，我们选择给他装上第二套软胎，这当然不是我们的基准选项。”
“不幸的是，正如你在第二阶段看到的那样，我们也遭遇了相当高的轮胎磨损，所以这可能是我们需要一起复盘的事情之一，为什么我们在第二阶段磨损得那么厉害。”
不过，梅基斯认为，无论选择什么策略，安东内利的速度优势都意味着他无论如何都会赢——而红牛传统上在较软配方上表现更好。
“可以说，与竞争对手相比，我们通常在较软配方上享有一点优势，但今天我们很难利用这一优势，”他说。
“我们为马克斯使用了两套较软配方，磨损相当高，这当然无助于我们落实第二次进站。”
维斯塔潘确实认为，红牛被拖入了一个基于其赛车在最近几场比赛中使用软胎表现良好而做出的决定。
他说：“有一刻很明显，使用更硬配方轮胎的人找到了很多抓地力，所以我想我们也没有真正对此做出反应。”
“可能只是过于坚持我们过去两场比赛的信念，当时更软的配方是最快的，而显然在这里那没有奏效。”
关于无线电问题，梅基斯表示，红牛对于为何连续第二场比赛遭遇这个问题感到困惑，但表示现在修复它是优先事项。
他说：“如果我们真的弄明白了，那问题早就解决了。所以我们并不完全清楚为什么会受到这些问题的影响。”
“当然，我必须承认竞争对手比我们做得更好，因为我们显然能听到所有人的无线电，而我们一直挣扎得比我们希望的要更多。”
他补充道：“这让每个人的日子都非常难过，所以这确实是我们希望尽快解决的问题，因为这是一个本应正常工作、不应耗费我们太多精力的事项。”
关于起步不佳以及哈贾尔提出需要重新设计离合器的建议，梅基斯认为这更像是2027年的项目，而非短期内的任务。
起步依赖于包括发动机、变速箱和离合器在内的多种元素的组合，因此这不是能够快速解决的问题。
因此，尽管可以继续改进以尽量减少问题，但在明年年初之前不太可能有更大的修复。
梅基斯补充道：“尽管我们已经缩小了与竞争对手的差距，你可能还记得我们年初的起步有多糟糕，但我们仍然不是标杆。”
“事实上，赛车在此期间有了很大改进，并且更接近前排竞争，这使得现在的这一劣势更加痛苦，因为我们周围的竞争非常激烈。
"一方面，我有信心从现在到年底我们会继续缩小与竞争对手的差距，因为每一场比赛我们都在学习，每一场比赛我们都能找到缩小差距的小方法。
"另一方面，我同样清楚，在赛季结束前我们不会成为标杆，这需要一些重大的设计和硬件改动，而这是我们只有到明年才会看到的事情。"
detailEn: Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar let rip at Red Bull after Formula 1's United States Grand Prix for a series of avoidable problems that left them unable to fully capitalise on the potential of their car.
Things went wrong at the start as Verstappen and Hadjar in particular made poor getaways from second and third on the grid.

The pair were then hampered throughout the race by radio problems that made communication with the pitwall difficult, while Verstappen was annoyed about the choice of a two-stop strategy that left the door open for the one-stopping Kimi Antonelli to take a dominant win.

Despite a radio message from team principal Laurent Mekies immediately after the chequered flag confessing the team had "a few things to tidy up", it was clear that frustrations were high in the cockpit.
In a bleak post-race radio message after taking the chequered flag in third, Verstappen said: "Terrible: the pace, the wrong tyre, sh** pitstop, sh** engine braking. Nothing worked."

Speaking to Viaplay after the race about whether he agreed on the strategy call in committing to softs for the second stint when the harder compounds appeared to be in play, Verstappen said: "No, it wasn't agreed upon. That's why I don't get it. Then everyone would know we're doing a two-stop."

Later on, referencing struggles with balance and engine braking that were not helped by the ongoing radio problems, Verstappen sarcastically told the media: "Maybe we just start communicating in sign language. It's probably cheaper as well.
"It's a disaster. It's really frustrating, to be honest."
Hadjar was even angrier, as he suggested that Red Bull needed a new clutch design because of the repeated weak starts.
"It needs a redesign because at the moment it's too fragile," said Hadjar, who eventually came home sixth. "It's not coping well with temperatures. It's a real struggle."
And then he expressed bafflement about why a relatively simple thing such as the team radio was such a frustrating issue.
"At the moment it's the little things we can't do," he said. "I have a poor radio, I don't even know what's happening. I dropped the clutch, it's going into a nightmare.
"We fix these two already, we might be on the podium. The hardest things it seems like we can do, and the silly things we can't."
Mekies was well aware of the issues that turned a possible victory challenge into a frustrating afternoon for his drivers.

On Verstappen's strategy call, Red Bull said it needed to analyse why the degradation on that second stint had been so poor, considering that the opening part of the race against Antonelli had appeared to be quite evenly matched.

Asked about Verstappen's complaints, Mekies said: "I'm not sure what he was referring to, because I didn't hear what he said, but I think one thing that may have surprised him is the fact that we elected to put him in the second set on softs, [it] was certainly not the baseline option for us.

"Unfortunately, as you have seen in that second stint, we also suffered a fairly high degradation, so it was probably one of the things we will review together, on why we degraded that much in that second stint."
Mekies felt, however, that whatever strategy was chosen Antonelli’s pace advantage meant he would have won anyway - and Red Bull has traditionally gone better on the softer compounds.
"It's probably fair to say that we normally enjoy a bit of an advantage compared to competition with the softer compounds, and today we have struggled to use that advantage," he said.
"We have suffered some fairly high deg with Max on the two sets of softer compounds that we had, and that certainly didn't help materialising the second stop."
Verstappen certainly thought Red Bull had got sucked into a call based on how well its car had run on softs in recent races.
"At one point it was quite clear that the people on the harder compounds were finding a lot of grip, so I guess we also didn't really react to that," he said.
"Just probably sticking too much to our belief from the last two races, where the softer compounds were the fastest, and clearly here that didn't work."
On the radio issue, Mekies said that Red Bull was confused about why it had been hit with this problem for the second race running, but said it was now a priority to fix.
"If we were understanding it, we would have solved it," he said. "So we don't fully understand why we are being hit by these issues.
"Certainly, I have to admit that the competition is doing a better job than us, because we can obviously hear everyone's radio, and we have been struggling more than what we would have liked to."

He added: "It's making everyone's lives very difficult, so it is true that it's something that we would like to fix quite quickly, because it's an item that should be working without using too much of our energy."
In terms of the poor starts and Hadjar's suggestion of the need for a clutch redesign, Mekies thought this was more a project for 2027 than the short term.
With starts reliant on a combination of elements - including engine, gearbox and clutch - it is not something that can be quickly addressed.
So while improvements could continue to be made to minimise the problems, a bigger fix is unlikely before the start of next year.
Mekies added: "As much as we have reduced the gap to competition, and you may remember how bad our starts were at the beginning of the year, we are still not the benchmark.
"The fact that the car in the meantime improved a lot, and is fighting closer to the front, makes that deficit even more painful now, because competition around us is very strong.

"On one side I'm confident that we will continue to reduce the gap to the competition from now to the end of the year, because every race we learn, every race we come up with small ways to close the gap.

"On the other side, I equally know that we will not be the benchmark before the end of the season, that it will require some significant design and hardware changes, and that this is something that we will see only next year."

items.originalTitle: Winners and losers from F1's United States Grand Prix
detailZh: F1美国大奖赛赢家和输家
随着他的第九场胜利让基米·安东内利接近首次夺冠，他的队友乔治·拉塞尔在美国大奖赛中更加陷入绝望
奥斯汀的F1赛事并非瞬间经典之作，这有些不幸，因为所有的元素都在那里。四支车队相对接近，三种轮胎配方都派上了用场，促使不同策略之间的较量
但美国赛车场对冠军基米·安东内利几乎没有办法让他这个20岁的年轻人动摇，因为他几乎可以保证下周日在墨西哥书写历史
随着刘易斯·汉密尔顿和乔治·罗素刚刚做到足以保持理论上的冠军争夺，没有人比安东内利在德克萨斯州做得更接近锁定交易了。
汉密尔顿和罗素下周在墨西哥都必须获胜，根据我们的数学计算这是不可能的，即使其中一人真的在墨西哥城高原获胜，安东内利也只需要挽救一分或两分，就能成为F1历史上最年轻的冠军，比塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔年轻整整三年。
托托·沃尔夫宣布安东内利在奥斯汀的胜利是他最好的，尽管从较慢的中胎开始，但他抵抗了早期的压力，然后简单地控制了局势，不受战略游戏技巧的影响，因为他和梅赛德斯坚持他们的计划进行一次进站。
在所有的兴奋中，沃尔夫可能忘记了安东内利在蒙扎的主场上的惊人反击胜利，这导致了法拉利车迷罕见地为银箭欢呼的场景。
关于安东内利的冠军庆祝活动，梅赛德斯提前准备的T恤、彩带和几加仑的香槟现在不得不移至墨西哥的首都。也许这是最好的选择。墨西哥的法定饮酒年龄是18岁而不是21岁...
比赛开始前，梅赛德斯的车库，媒体纷纷涌向即将成为冠军的安东内利
抛开玩笑不谈，拉塞尔在最近几场比赛中已经达到了新的低谷，很难弄清楚具体原因。即使你认为安东内利本质上比拉塞尔更快或更优秀，证据开始逐渐增多，但拉塞尔也不比意大利车手慢很多，所以肯定还有其他原因。
一种理论是，梅赛德斯在马来西亚的升级，使得赛车更快，但也更难发挥和进入最佳性能窗口，这 somehow 影响了拉塞尔比安东内利更多。一旦梅赛德斯W17没有按照他的意愿行事，拉塞尔似乎比他的经验较少的对手更容易跌入谷底。
“六圈好成绩，五十圈糟糕成绩。我想知道为什么第一圈的速度这么慢，”拉塞尔在完成第八名后抱怨道，他后面跟着同样挣扎的麦克拉伦车手奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里。
“有一些迹象表明，调整窗口非常小。我希望这可以解释我今天缺乏速度的原因，但我需要和我的团队深入挖掘，因为当你落后这么多时，很难理解。”
“在这个时候，拉塞尔也注定要输给汉密尔顿，对于这位英国人来说，主要任务是止血，找到一些可行的解决方案，以便在赛季结束后比现在处于更好的位置。”
“两周前，勒克莱尔因为在新加坡的谨慎起步而受到批评，当时他有机会在第一圈超越杆位车手马克斯·维斯塔潘，但他退缩了。”
无论那次错失的机会是否影响到了他的心态，奥斯汀在勒克莱尔巧妙地从荷兰人的外侧绕过COTA赛道第一个精彩弯道时，几乎没有犹豫。
“是的，那很有趣，”勒克莱尔说。“我并不真的知道结果会怎样。那很接近，但很有趣。”
他和法拉利车队用一场更加强劲的比赛弥补了另一场没有达到预期结果的排位赛，并在比赛的最后三分之一中再次超越了维斯塔潘，因为他获得了轮胎寿命的优势。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔和马克斯·维斯塔潘在奥斯汀对决的开始阶段展开了车轮战。
伊萨克·哈迪尔在排位赛中尽管之前周末一直很艰难，但还是取得了不错的成绩，但他的比赛在周日迅速崩溃。
"我只是看着我的比赛开始," 他说。"在程序方面一切都很完美，然后我出现了离合器过度供油的情况。这些我无法控制的事情，它开始……我的无线电覆盖不好，我听不到发生了什么。我带着错误的地图进入维修区，……我在那硬胎上每圈都要损失一秒。
当他从第三位发车下滑到第六位结束比赛时，哈迪尔的麻烦如此令人沮丧，以至于他逐渐在无线电中失去了冷静，让人想起了他在F2中的那个火爆脾气。
无线电的故障导致一些信息丢失，比如转向硬胎的动作让哈迪尔感到意外。最终结果是，由于各种超出法国人控制的问题，失去了登上领奖台的机会，这抵消了一些从艰难的周五恢复过来的出色工作。
“今天的节奏很好，这是最难的部分，”他总结道。“我们做到了。还有那些我们无法做到的小愚蠢的事情，我们同样需要做到。”
利亚姆·劳森是奥斯汀的出色表现者之一
利亚姆·劳森的美国大奖赛周末值得铭记，他在复杂的赛道上找到了正确的节奏，这让他离开了他的舒适区。但关于他在周四晚上作为歌手兼词曲作者的首场现场表演就足够了。他在赛道上的表现也毫不逊色。
劳森通过一场控制的驾驶将小红牛的连续积分完赛记录延长至六场，在科塔科尔奇斯赛道这一事件中，这位英意车队再次证明了自己是其他车队中的佼佼者，领先于阿尔派和奥迪。
在连续几次获得第六名之后，小红牛正朝着超越自我，确保其最佳 constructors' championship 结果迈进，目前102分领先阿尔派 33分。后者需要在2024年巴西大奖赛上重复其双领奖台奇迹才能扭转局势。
兰多·诺里斯在比赛结束前在车队无线电中的悲观、几乎苦涩的犹豫表现出了从过去两个赛季的大部分时间里拥有最快的赛车到成为第四快的赛车手的感觉。这并不有趣。'你想怎么做策略就怎么做吧'，这是诺里斯试图在磨损的硬胎上保持领奖台位置时的基本总结。
这是一次值得追求的赌注，尽管他最终获得了第五名，但并没有改变最终的结果。一旦离开赛车并恢复精力，诺里斯的态度就温和了一些。最终，迈凯伦并没有落后太多，因为F1 2026的前四名车队在全新规则的第一年里出人意料地非常接近。诺里斯甚至乐观地认为，如果他的排位赛圈速更好，他可能已经挽救了一个前排发车的位置。对于一个世界冠军来说，这并不容易接受突然的成功缺失。
与此同时，皮亚斯特里在2026款赛车上的困境仍在继续。在奥斯汀，由于赛车在他更喜欢的2025年已经是他最弱的赛道之一，因此在那里几乎没有进步的迹象，这并不令人惊讶。在海拔高度上，低抓地力赛道上也很常见打滑的墨西哥，可能对澳大利亚球迷来说又是一场艰难的比赛。
detailEn: Winners and losers from F1's United States Grand Prix
As his ninth win of the campaign brought Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a maiden crown, his team-mate George Russell was driven further to despair at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix

Austin's Formula 1 race was no instant classic, which was somewhat unfortunate because a lot of the ingredients were there. Four teams were relatively closely matched, and all three tyre compounds were in play to prompt a battle between different strategies.
But there was little the Circuit of the Americas could throw at winner Kimi Antonelli to unsettle the 20-year-old as he is now all but guaranteed to write history next Sunday in Mexico.
With both Lewis Hamilton and George Russell only just doing enough to stay in theoretical title contention, one can't get much closer to sealing the deal than Antonelli did in Texas.

Both Hamilton and Russell would have to win in Mexico next week, which according to our mathematical calculations is not possible, and even in the event that one of them does win on the Mexico City plateau, Antonelli will only need to salvage a point or two to become F1's youngest ever champion by three whole years, succeeding Sebastian Vettel.

Toto Wolff declared Antonelli's win in Austin his best, resisting early pressure despite starting on the slower medium tyre and then simply controlling affairs, unperturbed by strategic gamesmanship as he and Mercedes stuck to their planned one-stopper.
In all his euphoria, Wolff may have forgotten about Antonelli's sensational comeback win on home soil in Monza, leading to the rare scenes of Ferrari tifosi cheering on a Silver Arrow.

As far as Antonelli's title celebration is concerned, Mercedes pre-made t-shirts, confetti and gallons of bubbly will now have to be moved to Mexico's capital. Perhaps it's for the best. The drinking age in Mexico is 18 rather than 21...
Mercedes garages before the start of the race, as media gravitate towards champion-elect Antonelli

All joking aside, Russell has sunk to a new low in recent races and it's hard to figure out exactly why. Even if you believe Antonelli is intrinsically the quicker or better driver, of which evidence is starting to mount, Russell isn't miles off the Italian's pace either, so something else is going on.

One theory is that Mercedes' Malaysia upgrade, which made the car faster but also harder to exploit and get into the optimal performance window, has somehow affected Russell more than Antonelli. Once the Mercedes W17 doesn't do exactly as he pleases, Russell appears to fall off a cliff more easily than his less experienced counterpart.

"Six good laps, 50 bad laps. I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint," Russell lamented after finishing eighth, stuck behind an equally struggling McLaren driver Oscar Piastri.

"There are signs that the set-up window is very small. I hope that's an explanation for my lack of pace today, but I need to dig deep with my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off."

With Russell also set to lose second to Hamilton at this point, the main priority for the Briton is to stop the bleeding and find some workable solutions to head into the off-season in a better place than he is now.
A fortnight ago Leclerc was criticised for his cautious start in Singapore, when he had a potentially race-defining opportunity to pass polesitter Max Verstappen into Turn 1 but backed out of it.

Whether that missed chance played on his mind or not, there was little hesitance in Austin as Leclerc deftly swooped around the outside of the Dutchman through the sweeps of COTA's magnificent first sector.
"Yeah, that was fun," Leclerc said. "I didn't really know how it would go. It was quite close, but it was fun."

He and Ferrari made up for another qualifying session that didn't yield the expected result with a stronger race, and was able to pass Verstappen again in the final third of the race as he banked a tyre life advantage.
Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen battled wheel-to-wheel at the start of the Austin showdown
Isack Hadjar snatched a great result in qualifying despite what had been a difficult weekend until that point, but his race swiftly unravelled on Sunday.

"I'm just watching my race start," he said. "Everything was perfect in terms of procedure and then I had a clutch overdelivery. And these things that are just out of my control, it's starting... I have poor radio coverage, I can't hear what's happening. And I hit the pits with the wrong map and... I'm losing a second on every lap on that hard tyre."
As he slumped to finish sixth from third on the grid, Hadjar's issues were so frustrating that he gradually lost his cool over the radio, bringing back flashes of that old hothead in F2.

The radio hiccups meant some things were lost, like the pivot to a hard tyre which caught Hadjar by surprise. The end result was a lost opportunity to be on the podium through various issues outside of the Frenchman's control, negating some of the excellent work that had been done to recover from a tough Friday.
"The pace was good today, that's the hard part of it," he summed up. "We nailed it. And all the little, stupid things we can't. We need to nail them as well."
Liam Lawson was one of the stand-out performers in Austin

Liam Lawson's United States Grand Prix weekend is one to remember, hitting the right notes on tricky terrain that left him out of his comfort zone. But enough about his live debut as a singer-songwriter on Thursday night. His on-track performance was nothing to scoff at either.

Lawson extended Racing Bulls' run of consecutive points finishes to six with a controlled drive to ninth, with COTA another event where the Anglo-Italian team proved to be best of the rest ahead of Alpine and Audi.

After several sixth-place finishes, Racing Bulls is well on its way to going one better and secure its best-ever constructors' championship result, its 102 points now leading Alpine by 33 points. The latter will need a repeat of its double podium miracle at the 2024 Brazilian Grand Prix to turn the tide.

Lando Norris' cynical, almost bitter reluctance on the team radio towards the end of the race showed what it's like to go from having the fastest car for much of the past two seasons to being fourth fastest. It's no fun. 'Do whatever you want with the strategy', is a basic summary as Norris tried to hang onto a podium spot on worn hard tyres.

It was a gamble worth pursuing and didn't change much to the end result as he took fifth. Once out of the car and refreshed, Norris was a bit milder. At the end of the day, McLaren isn't miles away as F1 2026's four top teams are surprisingly closely matched during the first year of all-new regulations. Norris even optimistically felt he could have salvaged a front-row start with a better qualifying lap. For a reigning world champion, that doesn't make the sudden absence of success easier to take, though.

Meanwhile, Piastri's struggles with the 2026 car continue. It should come as no great surprise there were few signs of progress in Austin, as it had already been one of his weakest circuits in 2025 when the car was generally more to his liking. Mexico, where sliding is also very common at altitude on the low-grip track, will likely be another tough watch for Australian fans.

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday
How can Kimi Antonelli become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history this Sunday at the Mexico City Grand Prix? Watch every session of the Mexico City GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win

Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City.
Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin to move 123 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate and nearest challenger George Russell, and 124 points ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris were officially knocked out of championship contention, leaving Russell and Hamilton as the only drivers who can technically prevent Antonelli from becoming the sport's youngest ever world champion at 20 years old.

In reality, Russell and Hamilton's chances are only technical, as one of them would need to win all five remaining races and for Antonelli to fail to score two points.
How Antonelli can win the 2026 F1 title at the Mexico City GP
There will be four scheduled races left - Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the Mexico City Grand Prix takes place this Sunday and a maximum of 100 points left to play for.
To win the title in Austin, Antonelli simply needs to score two points, or not be outscored by Russell by 23 points and Hamilton by 24 points.
The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Mexico City are:
Russell and Hamilton fail to win the race
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'
When can Mercedes clinch the Constructors' Championship?
Mercedes will also have a first mathematical chance to clinch the Constructors' Championship in Mexico - but securing that title next time out is a very tall order.
They lead Ferrari by 133 points in the standings and there will be 172 points left to play for after this Sunday's race.

To become champions in Mexico, they would need to outscore Ferrari by 39 points. This would require Antonelli or Russell winning the Grand Prix, with the other driver in second or third, plus a disastrous race for both Ferrari drivers.

The Silver Arrows' first realistic chance to wrap things up will therefore likely come at next week's Sao Paulo Grand Prix when they would only need to finish the Interlagos event 129 points ahead, four fewer than now.
However, Ferrari have outscored them at each of the last three race weekends.

Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix
Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso hit out at Williams' Alex Albon and stated the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid is "very low" after the pair collided at the United States Grand Prix.
Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.

"It was the best race by far of the year for us in terms of competitiveness. Good tyre management. We got a lot of damage on Lap 1 with the Albon incident," he said.
"Despite that, the car was still competitive. We had a P9 or P10 on merit. The best and strongest race of the year but ruined in the first lap with the Turn 11 incident."
Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon sit down with Sky Sports for a chat over Texas BBQ in Austin
Albon felt he did not need need to apologise for the collision with Alonso as Esteban Ocon was on the outside of the Spaniard and also played a role in the incident.
"It's racing. I think there was a car on his outside that squeezed [him]. I was side by side with him the whole way into the corner. It's hard to disappear," said the Williams driver.
"I thought we had some good racing. We had a second go at it later in the race. I enjoyed it at least. I hope he feels the same way on the second half. It was good fun."

items.originalTitle: Red Bull admits frustrating F1 problem will not be fully fixed until 2027
detailZh: 红牛承认F1问题将在2027年才能完全解决
红牛车队负责人劳伦特·梅基斯承认，车队在比赛开始时遇到的问题将在2027年才能完全解决。
对于红牛车队的粉丝来说，关注红牛赛车，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和比赛分析。
红牛车队负责人劳伦特·梅基斯承认，车队在比赛开始时遇到的问题将在下一赛季才能得到完全解决。这是在伊萨克·哈德贾在美国大奖赛艰难起步后呼吁重新设计离合器之后。
红牛车手在奥斯汀赛事的起跑时从第三位跌至第五位，哈德杰将原因归咎于"离合器提前释放"。更糟糕的是，他和队友马克斯·维斯塔潘都遭遇了无线电故障，后者开玩笑说车队应该"开始使用手语交流"。
梅克斯被问及哈德杰是否正确，他说他的车队擅长解决复杂问题，但不擅长解决"愚蠢的事情"。
他表示，伊萨克所说的话中有些是真实的，意思是我们都对连续两场比赛中无线电故障的困扰感到沮丧。"这使每个人的生活都非常困难，所以确实，我们希望尽快解决这个问题，因为它应该是一个不需要消耗太多能量的项目，所以他在这方面是正确的。"
他说，起跑是一个更严重的问题。
“起跑是一个稍微复杂的问题，意味着起跑表现几乎涉及到公司的所有部门，可能除了空气动力学。它是引擎，是变速箱，是离合器，是许多事情，而且我们从赛季开始就确实看到了，在起跑性能方面我们并不是标杆。”
他说，车队提高的节奏使得它的比赛起跑更加引人注目。
“你可能还记得我们年初起跑有多糟糕。我们仍然不是标杆。而且，是的，汽车在此期间有很大改进，并且更接近前方的竞争使得这种差距现在更加痛苦，因为周围的竞争非常激烈。”
但为了完全修复，车队粉丝将不得不等待。
“所以，关于你的观点，一方面，我对从现在到年底我们将继续缩小与竞争对手的差距充满信心，因为每一场比赛我们都在学习，每一场比赛我们都能找到缩小差距的小方法。另一方面，我也同样清楚，在赛季结束前，我们不会成为标杆，这需要一些重大的设计和硬件改动，而且这是明年我们才能看到的事情。”
在无线电问题上，法国人承认他们不明白问题根源在哪里。
“如果我们理解了，我们就会解决这个问题，所以我们不完全明白为什么我们会受到这些问题的困扰。当然，我必须承认，竞争者在我们的表现上做得更好，因为我们显然能听到每个人的无线电，而我们比我们希望的更努力地挣扎。”
detailEn: Red Bull admits frustrating F1 problem will not be fully fixed until 2027
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has admitted the team's race start problems will not be fully resolved until 2027
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has admitted that the issue the team has faced at the start of races won't be fixed until next season. This comes after Isack Hadjar called for the clutch to be redesigned following a difficult start to his United States Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver dropped from third to fifth as the lights turned off at the start of the Austin race, with Hadjar blaming "clutch over delivery". To make matters worse, both he and team-mate Max Verstappen suffered from radio issues, with the latter joking that the team should "start communicating in sign language".
Mekies was asked whether Hadjar was right when he said his team was good at fixing complex issues, but not "silly things".

“I think there is some truth in what Isack is saying, meaning we are all frustrated to struggle for the second race in a row with the radio issues," he told the media. "It’s making everyone’s lives very difficult, so it is true that it’s something that we would like to fix quite quickly because it’s an item that should be working without using too much of our energy, so he’s right on that one.”
The starts, he said, are a more substantial problem.

“The start is a slightly more complex issue to solve, meaning that the start performance is going across pretty much all the departments of the company, probably except aerodynamic. It’s engine, it’s gearbox, it’s clutch, it’s many things, and we certainly have seen from the beginning of the season that we are not the benchmark in term of launch performance.”
He said the team’s improved pace has made its race starts more noticeable.

“And you may remember how bad our starts were at the beginning of the year. We are still not the benchmark. And yes, the fact that the car in the meantime improved a lot and is fighting closer to the front makes that deficit even more painful now because competition around us is very strong.”
But for a full fix, fans of the team will have to wait.

“So to your point, on one side I’m confident that we will continue to reduce the gap to the competition from now to the end of the year because every race we learn, every race we come up with small ways to close the gap. On the other side, I equally know that we will not be the benchmark before the end of the season, that it will require some significant design and hardware changes, and that this is something that we will see only next year.”
On the radio problems, the Frenchman admitted that they don't understand where the issue stems from.

“If we were understanding it we would have solved it, so we don’t fully understand why we are being hit by these issues. Certainly I have to admit that competition is doing a better job than us because we can obviously hear everyone’s radio, and we have been struggling more than what we would have liked to.”
